name: Jirajaran
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. & Pieter C. Muysken. 2004. The Languages of the Andes. Cambridge: CUP, §2.14 Jirajaran, pp. 129-130.
new_statements.check: reported on verification, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Spot-checks of the two 'silent' works found nothing missed. Mason 1950: a full-text search for stress/accent (pp. 157-317) for stress/accent hits only Jivaro and Puinave, never Jirajara. Adelaar & Muysken 2004: 19 additional item-restricted full-text queries (Jirajaran+tone, Jirajaran+stress, Ayaman+syllable/accented/phonological, Gayon+stress, and phrase walks through §2.14) recover the section's sentences on peoples, history, sources, Siquisique, the 1910 Ayaman speakers, example (190) and the a-/an- prefix; no stress or accent sentence for Jirajaran appears, and all stress/accent/tone highlights sit in other chapters. Oramas 1916 remains blocked.

sources.note: Ayamán appears only in comparative word tables and a note on the Siquisique vocabulary; his 'acento es llano/grave' remarks concern Río Negro languages, not Ayamán.

sources.note: Nothing; classification only ('el ayamán-gayón era un idioma aislado; en cambio, el jirajara se nos presenta como un dialecto chibcha'); refers to his 1942 BSVCN study of the vocabularies.

sources.citation: Venezuela misionera (Caracas). 1939. '4. Familia Jirajara' (mission-magazine survey of Venezuelan language families).
sources.note: Nothing; ethnographic note naming Oramas 1916 and Jahn 1927 as the only studies.

sources.citation: Jahn, Alfredo. 1927. Los aborígenes del occidente de Venezuela: su historia, etnografía y afinidades lingüísticas. Caracas: Lit. y Tip. del Comercio. Vocabulario Ayomán pp. 379-387; Vocabulario Jirajara de Siquisique comparado con el Ayomán pp. 388-391; Vocabulario Gayón pp. 392-399.
sources.note: Nothing. Alphabet note p. 379 ('Hemos empleado en su escritura un alfabeto combinado, fonético') explains only h, sh, ch, ä, ö; forms are written with acute accents (a-tógh, a-kivóugh, a-hóui, tachát; my rough tally of the Ayomán list: 174 accent-marked form-lines, 143 final, 21 penult, 10 other) but no rule or remark on accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent acent/pronunci/sílaba: only the footnote on the pronunciation of the ethnonym Ayomán).

sources.citation: Arcaya, Pedro Manuel. 1920. Historia del Estado Falcón, tomo I. Caracas. Language chapter pp. c. 30-85.
sources.note: Only accent remark is on the Spanish-verse stress of the ethnonym Caquetío (p. 32); Jirajara classed as Betoi, Ayamán as Tupi; no Jirajaran stress statement.

sources.citation: Oramas, Luis R. 1916. Materiales para el estudio de los dialectos Ayamán, Gayón, Jirajara, Ajagua. Caracas: Litografía del Comercio. 68 pp.
sources.note: Primary Ayamán/Gayón/Jirajara wordlists and colonial surname lists (pp. 15-29 per Loukotka); the only place besides Jahn where an orthographic note on accent marks could exist. HathiTrust full view exists but this network is blocked.

sources.citation: Arcaya, Pedro M. 1906. Lenguas indígenas que se hablaron en el Estado Falcón. Capítulo preliminar. El Cojo Ilustrado (Caracas), 1 Aug 1906.
sources.note: Nothing; sets out a lexical-comparison programme for the Ayamán words; no phonology.
